author: dapplion
content: First I want to appreciate and celebrate your work all the zk teams work. I's absolutely crazy what has been achieved in such a short amount of time

author: dapplion
content: In your opinion and thinking ambitiously / long term, what's left to make eip8025 sound?

author: dapplion
content: Without recursion, a node that checkpoint syncs can't easily check validity of the payloads prior to the initial checkpoint sync block. CL clients are built on the assumption that ELs do that in the background with optimistic sync. Changing this would be a quite big refactor. This is a strong argument for recursive IMO

author: dapplion
content: Zisk team claims that the can easily do recursion today with 200ms of added latency and it's something they want anyway for the other systems using their proofs (rollups)

author: dapplion
content: Without recursion we need to implement proof sync in Lighthouse, which is a significant effort of ~5k lines, plus having to persist proofs bloating storage (retention window x supported proofs types (say 4) x ~0.25-1MiB = 7-29 GB / day based on retention period
